I have been following this games since months, finally I made that hard decision of taking a risk of buying an Early Access game (I just Hate Early access games).
However, I found that this was really worth the investment.
Kenshi is a genre in itself. You are thrown with a single player (or a group depending upon your choice of gameplay at startup), to live in a harsh world. Now it is upto you as to how you play and what your objectives are. You can buy backpacks and bulls and be a trader, or you can create industries and be an industrialist. You may choose to become a fighter and hire and train other fighters, to create a fighting squad and boast your power upon the world, or you might want to be an ordinary man (or women) trying to survive and live in this world.
On the downside, the game is an unfinished product and has performance issues (The devs have promised to improve performance significantly in coming days), and bugs. But it is still very playable and appears like a Beta version, though it is listed as alpha.

Great game for sure. It can be improved in many aspects.
Leaving aside the graphic section and the engine (which is the worst thing about the game).
-A relationship system between the characters could be added to give it more depth, perhaps playing with some personalities.
-More styles of martial arts, some more focused on defense or attack, with different animations.
-The game's own taming system. This would include mounts as well.
-Some type of junk vehicle to be able to make nomadic bases.
-Personal vehicles such as sand sliders.
-There are countless mods that are great. They should add them to the base game like others have already done.
I hope to see some of these things and more in Kenshi 2

Found this game by chance based on random YouTube videos and do not regret it. The game is enjoyable to play in my honest opinion.
The difficulty of this game is the thing that puts many people off. Yes the game can be difficult and there is a slight grind before you are strong enough to not die to everything. Don't let that put you off. The game is great.
The game is in early access and as such, may change at a later date. However, as it is, I would recommend getting this game.
Also, the game includes the Forgotten Construction set. Essentially allowing you to mod your own game. And it is not hard to understand either.
This game is an easy 9/10.

EDIT:
Game is out of early access for a little while now and still maintains the fun but difficult gameplay that first got me interested in the game. The game has not changed much outside of early access and while the developers are supporting the game, their newly announced Kenshi 2 means that this game is unlikely to get more then small updates focused on removing bugs and minor optimisations.
Would still recommend.

It's a hard game to recommend. Do you like indie survival sandboxes with outpost and squad tactical management? A world with all the worldbuilding and lore, but no actual story beyond the one you tell yourself? Do you enjoy looking on reddit and steam forums to learn all the complexities that are never explained in game? If you answered yes, or think that they are at least, not a deal breaker, then this is the perfect game for you.

It's easy to get lost hundreds of hours in it, I personally enjoy leading just one guy and training them into a god of war. However, you can create a group of friends or even rule a city, if that's your thing. My end goal of every run is to burn the Holy Nation to the ground and lead a group of lady ninjas to victory. But there are always hundreds of hours and different ways for me to get there.

Interesting and fun.

Pros:

- World feels like it lives and breathes, your decisions have consequences, both for you and the world
- Lore is deep enough yet short enough to not become a wall of text
- Excelent combat system
- Excelent skill development system
- Nice construction system
- Sheer flexibility

Cons:

- Interactions with NPCs could be better. Example: I thought guard to be dead, tried to strip him, guard woke up, skreamed 'thief', resulted in trader refusing to trade with me forever and refusing to trade with squadmates he never saw before. He still doesn't trade after my squad became strong enough to wipe the floor with the trader and his guards. There is no way to pay reparations or force the issue with either violence, intimidation or reputation
- Some UI elements could be better
- There are some odd limitation with cities
- Production is surprisingly inflexible, ex: no production limits for things like construction materials or food, it goes on untill all relevant inventories are full or all raw resources are used up.
- Some minor bugs are still around, but arguably that's expected with the game of this scope
- State of the game in relation to ranged weapons is kinda odd, effectively everything is melee or at the range of a thrown knife, it is notiecebale, but doesn't clash with the setting too much.

You can do literally whatever you want, and the world doesn't care. It's open world in the truest sense.

But if you go into this game with the desire to create your own internal story and make your owl goals, you will literally never be able to put it down, and can easily sink hours upon hours into this game.

Highly recommended.

Kenshi is a RPG-RTS featuring a slow progression and massive learning curve. It's core features, being RTS battles and Dwarf Fortress-like base building, are made more complex with every patch. Though, it does lack somethings, for instance: The beginning starts you out fairly weak, even the beginnings geared towards making you more combat ready only leave you with a powerful weapon against an army of more experienced bandits.

The difficulty fluctuated heavily a few hours in though. Even after amassing an army, you still aren't strong enough to take on a single bandit party. However, when you reach a point, and you've leeched a few kills off of guards with your squad of cowards, you're able to leave the game running with no fear of attack -- or agency. I'd automated an entire camp. Random events and the like, a feature of base-building games that it emulates, would and have been a boon.

This game could easily be the greatest game I ever play -- the potential is there. I need that 3D dwarf fortress.

It's definitely been said before, but what makes this game so great is that there are no rails to stay on. You are nobody and you are free to make of that what you will. Any attempt to fix the state of the world will only make it worse, and any attempt to destroy it will come with strong opposition. Story isn't forced upon you but you can scrape together what may have happened by speaking with people who come with their own biases, or through the environment that survives past catastrophes. It might not be for everyone but I think if sandbox RPGs sound fun to you it might be worth a try.

I've had this game since MAY 2014 - I have enjoyed it everytime I play it. If your into sandbox/openworld/RPG this game should be in your library or on your wish list. Tons of hours worth of gameplay for a game in Alpha.

THE GAME ITSELF: I prefer to start off on hardest mode - with nothing. Start off scrounging for goods off dead bandits after leading them towards guards to kill them fo me. Slowly gathering resources, buildings, hiring teammates, occasionally getting my a$* kicked by dogs or other enemies (quicksave is very useful here) - but the build up and effort delivers reward.
HOWEVER - the game seriously is in need of some kind of storyline. I like to play towards an end goal, and at presen I am somewhat lacking this.

Development of the game e.g. new enemies, AI, buildings are steadily released along with bug fixes so developers are always active. If you need proof of the work being done just check out recent updates part of page.

Overall its a very good game to play through its development. Definitely worth the money in my opinion.

Pretty much, do what you want. If you cant do it, theres a mod that will let you. After 100 hours, I even started making my own mods/tweaks to fit my gameplay. Literally, endless RP opportunities. If you want to name yourself "Bob", and survive a world without arms and legs.. You can do it. Want to open a hashish cafe, sit around smoking a hookah, while waiting for customers? Yep, I did that too. Meanwhile a psychopath skeleton, who believes hes a human (wearing a skin suit), runs my slave hemp farm with an iron fist! *literally*. Regardless of your wants for adventure, this game will weirdly fill the gap. Inspiration will come at every new discovery. Then when you discover you CANT do what you want, theres probably a mod that'll make you say, "I CAN!"

But yes, this is a game that you SHOULD mod. You dont need to download game breaking things, but simple as recruiting prisoners are great new player features that will fill the gaps between "Base game Impossible" to "Endless Fun!"

This game is phenomenal. There is a gameplay loop you'll never ever find in any other game.

It it worth noting that loop is not for everyone. If the phrase "losing is fun" makes you want to refund a game, don't even consider diving into the world of Kenshi.

Otherwise you will have a good time exploring the world and exploiting it in many disticnt ways. There is a lot to do and discover and after that you are going to realise that there is a ton of quality mods which shape the world to your taste.

It can be a buggy and clumsy, the visuals are horrible for today standards, but there is no other game like Kenshi. So you just have to deal with it.

There also is a standalone game editor which is simple enough to tweak a lot of values to your liking yourself, which is also kind of cool, because it can also be used to fix ingame bugs. Where else can you make a DIY patch for a game to fix THAT pesky bug which personally bothers YOU and seemengly no one else?

10/10, one of the best games i've ever played.

Other than that, I can't express how much I enjoy this game and there is still more to come.
